attrs.management_says: The larger increase in accounts receivable ($90.8M incremental vs 2014) was primarily due to the timing of shipments.
attrs.numbers_show: Q4 2015 receivables jumped 55% year-over-year while Q4 revenue rose 30.8%; Q4 DSO rose from 28 to 34 days (E30). Full-year DSO rose from 33 to 40 days (E25), driven by the year-end snapshot. The incremental receivables increase (2015 Δ$153.8M vs 2014 Δ$65.1M ≈ $88.7M) aligns with the cited $90.8M.

attrs.management_says: Operating cash flow fell $263.1M to -$44.1M due to a $370.1M decrease in cash from operating assets/liabilities, driven by a $193.9M inventory increase (early deliveries for seasonal floor sets) and a $90.8M larger receivables increase (shipment timing).
attrs.numbers_show: CFO swung from +$219.0M to -$44.1M (E6, E18, E26). Management quantifies the working capital drag at $370.1M, with inventory ($193.9M) and incremental receivables ($90.8M) totaling $284.7M; the remainder comes from other operating assets/liabilities (E48, E49, E50). The numbers are consistent.

attrs.management_says: Accounts receivable increased $90.8M more in 2015 than in 2014 primarily due to the timing of shipments.
attrs.numbers_show: Receivables grew 55% ($279.8M → $433.6M) vs. revenue 28.5%; DSO rose 33→40 days. Q4 receivables jumped 55% YoY ($279.8M → $433.6M) with DSO rising 28→34 days, consistent with late-quarter shipments. The incremental YoY increase in receivables change is ~$88.7M, close to the cited $90.8M.

attrs.management_says: Revenue growth is attributed to demand drivers; shipment timing is only cited for receivables/cash flow, not for revenue.
attrs.numbers_show: The Q4 receivables spike (DSO 28→34) implies roughly 6 extra days of sales in year-end receivables. On Q4 revenue of $1,170.7M, that equals ~$65–78M of revenue potentially pulled forward into 2015 (7–9% of the $878.9M total growth). The bulk of growth remains demand-driven.

attrs.management_says: In 2014, the receivables increase was attributed to a higher proportion of international sales with longer payment terms.
attrs.numbers_show: International revenue grew 69% in 2015 (vs 2014), which would also lengthen DSO, but management's 2015 explanation cites only shipment timing, not payment terms.

attrs.reason: Quarterly data shows a sharp Q4 2015 receivables increase (55% YoY) versus a 30.8% revenue increase, with DSO rising from 28 to 34 days (E30). The Q4 spike supports a shipment-timing driver.
